title: Next.js 15 + Velite: Modern Content Management Solution
summary: Exploring the content management solution combining Next.js 15 with Velite, and why we chose this technology stack.
html:
Next.js 15 + Velite: Modern Content Management Solution

When building 8plus.app, I chose the Next.js 15 + Velite technology combination. This article shares the reasons for choosing this solution and practical experience.

Why Choose Velite?

1. Type Safety

Velite is based on Zod schema, providing complete TypeScript type support:

const posts = defineCollection({
  name: 'Post',
  pattern: 'content/posts/**/*.mdx',
  schema: s.object({
    title: s.string(),
    date: s.isodate(),
    tags: s.array(s.string()).optional(),
    summary: s.string(),
    published: s.boolean().default(true),
    content: s.mdx()
  })
})

2. Simple Yet Powerful

Compared to Contentlayer, Velite provides a cleaner API and better performance:

  • Faster build times
  • Less configuration
  • Better error messages

3. Next.js 15 Compatibility

Velite natively supports Next.js 15, avoiding version compatibility issues.

Practical Experience

Configuration File Structure

export default defineConfig({
  root: '.',
  output: {
    data: '.velite',
    assets: 'public/static',
    base: '/static/',
    clean: true
  },
  collections: { posts, projects },
  mdx: {
    rehypePlugins: [
      rehypeSlug,
      [rehypeAutolinkHeadings, { behavior: 'wrap' }]
    ]
  }
})

Using in React Components

import { posts } from '.velite'

export default function BlogPage() {
  const publishedPosts = posts
    .filter(post => post.published)
    .sort((a, b) => new Date(b.date).getTime() - new Date(a.date).getTime())
  
  return (
    <div>
      {publishedPosts.map(post => (
        <article key={post.slug}>
          <h2>{post.title}</h2>
          <p>{post.summary}</p>
        </article>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

Build Process

The build process is very simple:

velite && next build

Velite will:

  1. Scan MDX files
  2. Validate frontmatter
  3. Generate type definitions
  4. Compile content to JSON

Advantages Summary

  1. Developer Experience: Complete type support and intelligent hints
  2. Performance: Fast build and runtime performance
  3. Simplicity: Minimal configuration, maximum functionality
  4. Reliability: Data validation based on Zod

Conclusion

Next.js 15 + Velite is an excellent modern content management solution, especially suitable for:

  • Technical blogs
  • Documentation sites
  • Project showcases
  • Personal websites

If you're looking for a simple yet powerful content management solution, I highly recommend trying this combination.

title: Responsive Design Best Practices: From Mobile-First to Desktop Adaptation
summary: A comprehensive guide exploring core principles of responsive web design, from mobile-first strategies to cross-device user experience optimization.
html:
Responsive Design Best Practices: From Mobile-First to Desktop Adaptation

In modern web development, responsive design is no longer optional—it's essential. With users accessing websites from various devices, we need to ensure quality user experiences across all screen sizes.

Mobile-First Design Philosophy

Why Choose Mobile-First?

Mobile-first is not just a technical strategy, but a design philosophy:

  • Performance Optimization: Starting with small screens naturally focuses on core functionality and content
  • Progressive Enhancement: Gradually adding features for larger screens rather than removing them
  • User Behavior: Over 60% of website traffic comes from mobile devices

Implementing Mobile-First

/* Base styles (mobile devices) */
.container {
  padding: 1rem;
  max-width: 100%;
}

/* Tablet devices */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .container {
    padding: 2rem;
    max-width: 768px;
    margin: 0 auto;
  }
}

/* Desktop devices */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .container {
    padding: 3rem;
    max-width: 1200px;
  }
}

Key Breakpoint Strategy

Common Breakpoint Settings

Based on actual device usage patterns, we recommend these breakpoints:

Device TypeWidth RangeBreakpoint
Mobile< 768pxDefault
Tablet768px - 1023pxmd:
Desktop1024px - 1279pxlg:
Large Screen≥ 1280pxxl:

Tailwind CSS Practice

<div className="
  grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 p-4
  md:grid-cols-2 md:gap-6 md:p-6
  lg:grid-cols-3 lg:gap-8 lg:p-8
  xl:grid-cols-4
">
  {/* Content */}
</div>

Responsive Image Handling

Next.js Image Component

import Image from 'next/image'

function ResponsiveImage() {
  return (
    <Image
      src="/hero-image.jpg"
      alt="Hero Image"
      width={1200}
      height={600}
      className="w-full h-auto"
      sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, (max-width: 1200px) 50vw, 33vw"
      priority
    />
  )
}

Key Optimization Points

  1. Proper sizes attribute: Tell the browser the image display width at different screen sizes
  2. Priority loading: Use priority attribute for important images
  3. Format optimization: Automatically select WebP or AVIF formats

Responsive Typography

Fluid Font Sizes

.heading {
  font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem);
  line-height: 1.2;
}

.body-text {
  font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.125rem);
  line-height: 1.6;
}

Readability Optimization

  • Line Length Control: 45-75 characters per line for optimal reading experience
  • Line Height Adjustment: Use larger line heights on mobile devices (1.6-1.8)
  • Contrast: Ensure sufficient contrast between text and background

Interactive Element Adaptation

Touch-Friendly Design

.button {
  min-height: 44px; /* Apple's recommended minimum touch target */
  min-width: 44px;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  margin: 8px; /* Sufficient spacing to avoid accidental touches */
}

.nav-item {
  padding: 16px; /* Navigation items need larger touch areas */
}

Hover State Handling

/* Only show hover effects on devices that support hovering */
@media (hover: hover) {
  .button:hover {
    background-color: #0056b3;
    transform: translateY(-2px);
  }
}

Performance Optimization Strategies

Critical Rendering Path

  1. Inline Critical CSS: Styles needed for above-the-fold rendering
  2. Lazy Load Non-Critical Resources: Use loading="lazy"
  3. Preload Important Resources: <link rel="preload">

Code Splitting

// Dynamic component import
const HeavyComponent = dynamic(() => import('./HeavyComponent'), {
  loading: () => <div>Loading...</div>,
  ssr: false // If server-side rendering is not needed
})

Testing and Debugging

Development Tools

  1. Chrome DevTools: Device simulation and network throttling
  2. Lighthouse: Performance and accessibility assessment
  3. Real Device Testing: Actual device testing is irreplaceable

Key Metrics

  • First Contentful Paint (FCP): < 1.8s
  • Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): < 2.5s
  • Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): < 0.1

Case Study: 8plus Website

In developing the 8plus website, we adopted the following responsive strategies:

Navigation Design

// Desktop navigation
<nav className="hidden md:flex items-center space-x-6">
  {navigation.map((item) => (
    <Link key={item.href} href={item.href}>
      {item.name}
    </Link>
  ))}
</nav>

// Mobile navigation
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger className="md:hidden">
    <Menu className="h-6 w-6" />
  </SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">
    {/* Mobile navigation content */}
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>

Content Layout

<div className="
  container py-8 
  md:py-16
">
  <div className="
    grid gap-8 
    lg:gap-12 
    md:grid-cols-2
  ">
    {/* Responsive grid layout */}
  </div>
</div>

Future Trends

Container Queries

@container (min-width: 400px) {
  .card {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}

New Viewport Units

.hero {
  height: 100dvh; /* Dynamic Viewport Height */
  min-height: 100svh; /* Small Viewport Height */
}

Conclusion

The key to successful responsive design lies in:

  1. User-Centered Approach: Understanding user behavior on different devices
  2. Performance First: Ensuring good loading speeds on all devices
  3. Progressive Enhancement: Starting with basic functionality and gradually adding complexity
  4. Continuous Testing: Validating design effectiveness on real devices

Responsive design is not a one-time task, but an important aspect that requires continuous attention and optimization throughout the development process.

title: 響應式設計最佳實踐：從移動優先到桌面適配
summary: 深入探討響應式網頁設計的核心原則，從移動優先策略到跨設備用戶體驗優化的完整指南。
html:
響應式設計最佳實踐：從移動優先到桌面適配

在現代網頁開發中，響應式設計已經不再是可選項，而是必需品。隨著用戶使用各種設備訪問網站，我們需要確保在所有螢幕尺寸上都能提供優質的用戶體驗。

移動優先的設計理念

為什麼選擇移動優先？

移動優先（Mobile First）不僅僅是一種技術策略，更是一種設計哲學：

  • 性能優化：從小螢幕開始設計，自然會關注核心功能和內容
  • 漸進增強：逐步為更大的螢幕添加功能，而不是削減功能
  • 用戶行為：超過 60% 的網站流量來自移動設備

實踐移動優先

/* 基礎樣式（移動設備） */
.container {
  padding: 1rem;
  max-width: 100%;
}

/* 平板設備 */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .container {
    padding: 2rem;
    max-width: 768px;
    margin: 0 auto;
  }
}

/* 桌面設備 */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .container {
    padding: 3rem;
    max-width: 1200px;
  }
}

關鍵斷點策略

常用斷點設置

基於實際設備使用情況，建議使用以下斷點：

設備類型寬度範圍斷點
手機< 768px預設
平板768px - 1023pxmd:
桌面1024px - 1279pxlg:
大螢幕≥ 1280pxxl:

Tailwind CSS 實踐

  grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 p-4
  md:grid-cols-2 md:gap-6 md:p-6
  lg:grid-cols-3 lg:gap-8 lg:p-8
  xl:grid-cols-4
">
  {/* 內容 */}
</div>

圖片響應式處理

Next.js Image 組件

import Image from 'next/image'

function ResponsiveImage() {
  return (
    <Image
      src="/hero-image.jpg"
      alt="Hero Image"
      width={1200}
      height={600}
      className="w-full h-auto"
      sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, (max-width: 1200px) 50vw, 33vw"
      priority
    />
  )
}

關鍵優化點

  1. 適當的 sizes 屬性：告訴瀏覽器在不同螢幕尺寸下圖片的顯示寬度
  2. 優先載入：重要圖片使用 priority 屬性
  3. 格式優化：自動選擇 WebP 或 AVIF 格式

字體與排版響應式

流體字體大小

.heading {
  font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem);
  line-height: 1.2;
}

.body-text {
  font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.125rem);
  line-height: 1.6;
}

可讀性優化

  • 行長控制：每行 45-75 個字符為最佳閱讀體驗
  • 行高調整：移動設備使用較大的行高（1.6-1.8）
  • 對比度：確保文字與背景有足夠的對比度

交互元素適配

觸控友好設計

.button {
  min-height: 44px; /* Apple 建議的最小觸控目標 */
  min-width: 44px;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  margin: 8px; /* 足夠的間距避免誤觸 */
}

.nav-item {
  padding: 16px; /* 導航項目需要更大的觸控區域 */
}

懸停狀態處理

/* 只在支持懸停的設備上顯示懸停效果 */
@media (hover: hover) {
  .button:hover {
    background-color: #0056b3;
    transform: translateY(-2px);
  }
}

性能優化策略

關鍵渲染路徑

  1. 內聯關鍵 CSS：首屏渲染所需的樣式
  2. 延遲載入非關鍵資源：使用 loading="lazy"
  3. 預載入重要資源：<link rel="preload">

代碼分割

// 動態導入組件
const HeavyComponent = dynamic(() => import('./HeavyComponent'), {
  loading: () => <div>載入中...</div>,
  ssr: false // 如果不需要服務端渲染
})

測試與調試

開發工具

  1. Chrome DevTools：設備模擬和網路節流
  2. Lighthouse：性能和可用性評估
  3. Real Device Testing：實際設備測試不可替代

關鍵指標

  • First Contentful Paint (FCP)：< 1.8s
  • Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)：< 2.5s
  • Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)：< 0.1

實戰案例：8plus 網站

在 8plus 網站的開發中，我們採用了以下響應式策略：

導航設計

  {navigation.map((item) => (
    <Link key={item.href} href={item.href}>
      {item.name}
    </Link>

</nav>

// 移動版導航

  <SheetTrigger className="md:hidden">
    <Menu className="h-6 w-6" />
  </SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">

">

    grid gap-8 
    lg:gap-12 
    md:grid-cols-2
  ">
    {/* 響應式網格佈局 */}
  </div>
</div>

未來趨勢

Container Queries

@container (min-width: 400px) {
  .card {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}

新的視口單位

  height: 100dvh; /* Dynamic Viewport Height */
  min-height: 100svh; /* Small Viewport Height */

總結

響應式設計的成功關鍵在於：

  1. 以用戶為中心：理解不同設備上的用戶行為
  2. 性能優先：確保在所有設備上都有良好的載入速度
  3. 漸進增強：從基礎功能開始，逐步增加複雜性
  4. 持續測試：在真實設備上驗證設計效果

響應式設計不是一次性的工作，而是需要在整個開發過程中持續關注和優化的重要環節。

title: Architecture First: Why B2B Projects Need Boundaries Before Code
summary: In consulting engagements, the most common failure is not picking the wrong stack — it is sprinting without defined boundaries. A practical architecture-first checklist.
html:
Architecture First

Under pressure, teams often skip architecture and jump into sprints. It looks like progress — until API coupling, permission gaps, deployment drift, and UX state chaos show up mid-flight.

Four questions I ask first

title: Next.js 16.4 and the October security update: patch first, then Cache Components
summary: October brought a new Next.js minor and two critical RCE fixes in the same week. Who is affected, which version to move to, and what in 16.4 actually matters for teams.
html:
Next.js 16.4 and the October security update

In October 2026 Next.js shipped 16.4 (Oct 6) and an out-of-band security update (Oct 14) within about a week. The new features are worth a look, but the order matters: patch first, plan the upgrade second.

1. First: the October 14 security update

Three issues were fixed. Two are critical, unauthenticated remote code execution:

IssueSeverityWho is affected
RCE when a use cache function returns multiple typed arraysCriticalApp Router + Cache Components, 16.0.0–16.4.0
RCE in Image Optimization with SVG (upstream sharp)CriticalImage optimization running on glibc-based Linux
CPU-exhaustion DoS via Server ActionsHighApp Router with at least one Server Action

The patched releases are 16.4.1 (Active LTS) and 15.5.28 (Maintenance LTS). The first issue has no workaround, and the Next.js team recommends upgrading even if your app has no similar functions. For the image issue, the interim fix is making sure sharp is 0.35.5 or later.

pnpm add next@16.4.1   # 16.x
pnpm add next@15.5.28  # projects still on 15.5

How I would prioritise

  1. Inventory, don't guess. Write down the version, whether cacheComponents is on, whether there is any 'use server', and where image optimisation runs. It takes ten minutes and tells you whether this is a today fix or a next-sprint fix.
  2. Anything public-facing gets patched the same day. A patch or minor bump is far less risky than leaving it.
  3. Run a short smoke test before shipping. Routes, metadata, forms, images — a few representative pages are enough.

Take this site as an example: no Server Actions, no use cache, only local images, and on Workers it does not go through sharp. The exposure is small, but it still goes on the upgrade list. "Not used today" does not mean "not used next month".

2. Three things in 16.4 that actually matter

1. Cache Components is now the recommendation

From 16.4, the Next.js team recommends Cache Components for every app. create-next-app enables it by default, and it is slated to become the default in Next.js 17. The idea is to declare caching at the component level with 'use cache', replacing the implicit caching of earlier App Router versions.

For existing projects: don't bundle the rewrite with the version bump. Get to 16.4.x for the security fixes, then plan the Cache Components migration as its own piece of work.

2. ensureStatic: make "this page must be static" a rule

Useful for marketing pages, blogs and storefront listings. Declare it on a route or layout:

export const ensureStatic = 'navigation';

If someone accidentally adds a dynamic component to that page, the build fails. A performance and hosting-cost agreement becomes something CI enforces instead of something people remember.

3. Upgrade tooling designed for AI agents

This is the part I find most telling about where things are going:

  • next upgrade --agent prepares version-specific migration guides, codemods and verification steps for your coding agent.
  • experimental.agentUpgrade defaults to nudging you during next dev / next build about releases that fix known vulnerabilities.
  • Agent feedback lets an agent draft reports on framework problems, which you review before anything is sent.

The framework now assumes the one running the upgrade may be an agent, while keeping a human confirmation at every step. That matches the principle from AI Integration in Practice: automation can do the execution, but permissions and sign-off stay with people.

3. An upgrade checklist for teams

  • Check your version and whether it falls in 16.0.0–16.4.0
  • Search for 'use cache', 'use server' and next/image
  • Move to 16.4.1 or 15.5.28 and confirm sharp ≥ 0.35.5
  • Run build, smoke and SEO checks, then ship
  • Open a separate task to evaluate Cache Components and ensureStatic
  • Consider agentUpgrade: 'security' so future security releases surface on their own

Frameworks are moving faster than ever. What teams need is not to chase every feature, but a steady, repeatable upgrade rhythm. If you want help taking inventory or planning an upgrade, book a 30-minute intro.

title: Next.js 16.4 與 10 月安全更新：先補洞，再談 Cache Components
summary: 10 月 Next.js 一口氣出了新版本與兩個 Critical 等級的 RCE 修補。整理哪些網站受影響、該升到哪一版，以及 16.4 對團隊真正有意義的變化。
html:
Next.js 16.4 與 10 月安全更新

2026 年 10 月，Next.js 在一週內先後發布了 16.4（10/6）與一次非例行安全更新（10/14）。新功能值得看，但順序很重要：先補洞，再規劃升級。

一、先處理：10/14 安全更新

這次修補了三個問題，其中兩個是 Critical 等級的「未經驗證遠端程式碼執行」：

問題等級誰會受影響
use cache 函式回傳多個 typed array 時的 RCECriticalApp Router + Cache Components，16.0.0–16.4.0
Image Optimization 處理 SVG 時的 RCE（上游 sharp）Critical在 glibc Linux 上執行 Next.js 的圖片最佳化
Server Actions 造成 CPU 卡死的 DoSHighApp Router 且有至少一個 Server Action

官方修補版本是 16.4.1（Active LTS）與 15.5.28（Maintenance LTS）。第一個問題沒有替代方案，官方建議即使你「看起來沒用到類似寫法」也直接升級；圖片問題的暫時解法是確保 sharp ≥ 0.35.5。

pnpm add next@16.4.1   # 16.x
pnpm add next@15.5.28  # 仍在 15.5 的專案

我會怎麼排優先順序

  1. 先盤點，不要先猜。 列出版本、是否啟用 cacheComponents、是否有 'use server'、圖片最佳化跑在哪裡。這份清單十分鐘就能做完，卻決定這是「今天要修」還是「下個 sprint」。
  2. 有對外服務的專案當天升版。 補丁版本只升 patch / minor，風險遠低於放著不管。
  3. 升完跑一輪 smoke test 再上線。 路由、metadata、表單、圖片，各抓幾個代表頁就好。

以這個網站為例：沒有 Server Actions、沒有 use cache，圖片都是本地檔案、部署在 Workers 上不走 sharp，暴露面很小——但依然排進升級清單。「目前沒用到」不代表下個月也不會用到。

二、16.4 真正值得注意的三件事

1. Cache Components 成為官方推薦

16.4 起，官方建議所有 Next.js 專案採用 Cache Components，create-next-app 也預設開啟，並預告在 Next.js 17 成為預設。核心概念是用 'use cache' 在元件層級宣告快取，取代舊 App Router 那套隱性快取行為。

對既有專案，我的建議是：不要跟著版本一起大改。先升到 16.4.x 拿到安全修補，再獨立規劃 Cache Components 遷移。

2. ensureStatic：把「這頁一定要靜態」寫成規則

對行銷頁、部落格、電商列表這類網站很實用。在 route 或 layout 宣告：

export const ensureStatic = 'navigation';

只要有人不小心把動態元件放進這頁，build 會直接失敗。這是把效能與主機成本的約定，從口頭提醒變成 CI 會擋的規則。

3. 官方開始為 AI Agent 設計升級流程

這是我認為最有趨勢意義的部分：

  • next upgrade --agent：替你的 coding agent 準備版本對應的遷移指南、codemod 與驗證步驟。
  • experimental.agentUpgrade：預設在 next dev / next build 時提醒有資安修補的版本。
  • Agent feedback：agent 遇到框架問題時起草回報，由你審閱後才送出。

框架開始假設「升級的執行者可能是 agent」，但每一步仍保留人類確認。這跟我在AI 導入實戰提到的原則一致：自動化可以做執行，但權限與驗收要留在人手上。

三、給團隊的升級清單

  • 確認目前版本與是否落在 16.0.0–16.4.0
  • 搜尋 'use cache'、'use server'、next/image 的使用位置
  • 升到 16.4.1 或 15.5.28，確認 sharp ≥ 0.35.5
  • 跑 build、smoke、SEO 檢查後上線
  • 另開工作項目評估 Cache Components 與 ensureStatic
  • 視需要啟用 agentUpgrade: 'security'，讓之後的資安版本自動提醒

框架更新越來越快，團隊需要的不是追每個新功能，而是一套固定、可重複的升級節奏。如果你的專案需要協助盤點或規劃升級，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Field Note | Moving 8plus to Cloudflare Workers: vinext in practice and three gotchas
summary: vinext, Cloudflare's Vite-based reimplementation of the Next.js API, is now in beta. How I deployed my own site to it in parallel, which lines changed, and why Vercel stays as the fallback.
html:
Moving 8plus to Cloudflare Workers

In February, Cloudflare announced vinext: the Next.js API reimplemented on Vite, deployable to Workers with one command. It started as an "AI rebuilt Next.js in a week" experiment and has since reached beta. Frameworks decoupling from their hosting platforms is one of the front-end trends I'm watching most closely this year.

Rather than just read about it, I tried it on my own site.

Principle: run in parallel, don't replace

  • Keep the Next.js source and build as they are, and add a separate vite build for Workers.
  • Vercel stays as the rollback origin; DNS is not touched first.
  • Preview on *.workers.dev, pass the smoke and SEO tests, and only then attach www.8plus.app/* as a Worker Route.

What the inventory showed

This site is an App Router + Velite content site: no Server Actions, ISR or API Routes, and no Vercel-only services. That is exactly the kind of site where vinext is easiest to adopt. The one visible difference is that React's ViewTransition is currently a passthrough, so page transitions don't animate.

Three gotchas

  1. Date.now() is 0 during module initialisation. On Workers the clock doesn't advance while modules load. I filtered published posts at module top level, so every post looked future-dated and returned 404. Computing it per request fixed it, with no change to Next.js behaviour.
  2. Rewrites to static files run at a different phase. vinext checks public/ before afterFiles rewrites, which broke /tool/qrcode → qrcode.html. Moving it to beforeFiles solved it.
  3. Toolchain types collide. The Next.js type check picked up the Vite 8 config files and failed, so vite.config.ts and cloudflare.config.ts are excluded in tsconfig.

All three were small changes, but without page-by-page testing the first one would have made the whole blog quietly disappear.

An existing bug found along the way

One of the best side effects of a migration is being forced to look at the whole site again. The production robots.txt and sitemap.xml were pointing at localhost, because the deployment was missing the site-URL variable. Unrelated to the move, but an SEO gap that had gone unnoticed for a long time.

Status and next steps

  • www.8plus.app is now served by the Worker, and all 29 smoke checks plus the SEO tests pass.
  • The apex domain still redirects via Vercel; once things are stable I'll switch DNS and rehearse the rollback.

If you're thinking about leaving a platform or cutting hosting costs, my advice is to build a feature inventory first and pick the framework second. To talk through your situation, book a 30-minute intro.

title: Field Note｜把 8plus 搬上 Cloudflare Workers：vinext 實測與三個踩坑
summary: Cloudflare 用 Vite 重新實作 Next.js API 的 vinext 已進入 beta。這是我把自己的網站平行部署上去的過程、改了哪幾行，以及為什麼保留 Vercel 當退路。
html:
把 8plus 搬上 Cloudflare Workers

今年 2 月，Cloudflare 發表 vinext：用 Vite 重新實作 Next.js 的 API，可以一行指令部署到 Workers。它從「AI 一週重寫 Next.js」的實驗，到了今年已進入 beta。框架與部署平台開始脫鉤，是今年前端最值得觀察的趨勢之一。

與其只看新聞，我拿自己的網站實測。

原則：平行部署，不是替換

  • 保留 Next.js 原始碼與建置流程，另加一條 vite build 給 Workers。
  • Vercel 繼續當回滾源站，DNS 不先動。
  • 先用 *.workers.dev 預覽，跑完 smoke 與 SEO 測試，才把 www.8plus.app/* 掛上 Worker Route。

盤點結果

這個站是 App Router + Velite 的內容站：沒有 Server Actions、ISR、API Routes，也沒有用到 Vercel 專屬服務。這類網站正是 vinext 最好上手的情境。唯一明顯差異是 React 的 ViewTransition 目前只是 passthrough，換頁轉場不會動畫。

三個踩坑

  1. 模組初始化時 Date.now() 是 0。 Workers 在載入模組的階段時鐘不前進，我把「過濾已發布文章」寫在模組頂層，結果所有文章都被判定為未來日期而 404。改成每次請求時計算就解決，Next.js 行為不變。
  2. rewrite 到靜態檔的階段不同。 vinext 在 afterFiles rewrite 之前就檢查 public/，導致 /tool/qrcode → qrcode.html 失效。改放 beforeFiles 即可。
  3. 工具鏈型別互相打架。 Next.js 的型別檢查會掃到 Vite 8 的設定檔而失敗，需要在 tsconfig 排除 vite.config.ts 與 cloudflare.config.ts。

三個都是小改，但如果沒有逐頁測試，第一個問題會讓整個部落格默默消失。

順手抓到的既有問題

搬家最大的收穫之一，是被迫把網站重新看一遍：正式站的 robots.txt 與 sitemap.xml 輸出成 localhost，原因是部署環境少設了一個網站網址的變數。這跟搬遷無關，卻是放了很久沒人發現的 SEO 漏洞。

現況與下一步

  • www.8plus.app 已由 Worker 提供，29 項 smoke 與 SEO 測試全過。
  • apex 網域仍由 Vercel 轉址；觀察穩定後再切換 DNS，並演練回滾。

如果你也在評估「離開某個平台」或「降低主機成本」，我的建議是：先做一份功能盤點表，再決定框架。想討論你的情況，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: AI agents wrote 30% more code, and teams shipped no more: the bottleneck is code review
summary: A Harvard study of more than 700 software firms found that AI coding agents raised code, commits and pull requests, but the number of completed issues did not move. What the study shows, and where teams should invest instead.
html:
AI agents wrote 30% more code, and teams shipped no more

In mid-October, Ars Technica covered a Harvard working paper by Fiona Chen and James Stratton (not yet peer reviewed). The headline is blunt: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software.

It is worth five minutes because it does not rely on surveys or lab tasks. It uses real work records from real companies.

1. How the study works

  • Data: telemetry from an engineering analytics platform, covering more than 700 software firms and about 300 million work events from 2021 to March 2026.
  • Method: firms adopted AI tools at different times, so the study compares adopters with firms that had not adopted yet, before and after adoption.
  • Two kinds of tools: autocomplete-style coding assistants, and coding agents that take a task and produce changes on their own.

2. The result: more upstream, flat downstream

After adopting coding agents, the average engineer produced:

MetricChange
Lines of codeabout +30% (nearly 1,500 extra lines a month)
Commitsabout +20%
Pull requestsabout +23%
Completed Jira issuesno statistically significant change

Headcount at the firm level did not drop noticeably either. The authors conclude that the productivity gains do not fully pass through to software output or employment. Constraints further down the process absorb them.

3. Absorbed where? Code review

The most interesting numbers in the coverage are on the review side:

  • Time from PR submission to merge rose about 49%
  • The share of PRs with changes requested nearly doubled
  • Review comments per PR rose about 35%
  • The share of engineers doing code review rose about 14%

Writing code got faster, but reviewers got busier, more work was sent back, and waits got longer. By March 2026 about 80% of firms used some form of AI code review, yet AI accounted for only 23.3% of review comments and appeared on 10.8% of PRs. Review is still mostly done by people.

The authors' advice is clear: to get the benefits of AI, firms need complementary investment in downstream review capacity, not just more code.

4. How I read it: this is not "AI doesn't work"

It is easy to read this as "AI coding is hype." I don't. What it really says is that software delivery is a production line. Speed up one station and the line still moves at the pace of the slowest one.

That matches the principle in my AI workflow integration post: automation can take over execution, but acceptance and permissions stay with people. Once execution gets cheap, acceptance becomes the new bottleneck.

Limits to keep in mind:

  • It is a working paper and has not been peer reviewed.
  • "Completed issues" is a coarse output measure. Quality, maintainability and incident rates are not counted.
  • The data ends in March 2026, and agents and AI review tools have improved a lot since.

5. Four changes for teams

1. Stop measuring the gain in lines and commits

The study points out that many managers rely on these intermediate metrics. They will always rise after adopting agents, and that does not mean more is shipped. Track lead time (ticket to production), review wait time per PR and the rate of PRs sent back instead.

2. Make PRs smaller and easier to review

Agents happily change a lot at once. Say it plainly in your guidelines or AGENTS.md: one PR does one thing, includes verification steps, and explains what changed and why. A PR that is easy to review is worth more than extra code.

3. Leave mechanical checks to CI, and keep people for judgment calls

Types, lint, tests, build and security scans should all run before a PR reaches a person. Human review time is for architecture, edge cases and business logic, the items on my code review checklist.

4. Plan review as real capacity

If agents add 20% more PRs, budget the review time to match instead of quietly pushing it onto senior engineers' evenings. AI review can do the first pass, but the final approval needs a named owner.

AI tools have made writing code cheap. The advantage has moved to confirming the code is right and shipping it safely. If your team feels busier since adopting AI but isn't shipping any faster, book a 30-minute intro call and we can find the station that's holding things up.

title: AI Agent 讓程式碼多了三成，交付卻沒變多：瓶頸其實在 Code Review
summary: 哈佛一份橫跨 700 多家軟體公司的研究發現：導入 AI coding agent 後，程式碼、commit、PR 都明顯增加，但完成的 issue 數沒有顯著變化。整理研究重點，以及團隊該把投資放在哪裡。
html:
AI Agent 讓程式碼多了三成，交付卻沒變多

10 月中，Ars Technica 報導了一份哈佛工作論文（Fiona Chen、James Stratton，尚未經同儕審查）。標題很直白：AI coding agent 產出更多程式碼，但沒有產出更多軟體。

這份研究值得花五分鐘看，因為它用的不是問卷或實驗室任務，而是真實公司的工作紀錄。

一、研究怎麼做

  • 資料：工程分析平台的遙測資料，涵蓋 700 多家軟體公司、約 3 億筆工作事件，時間從 2021 年到 2026 年 3 月。
  • 方法：各公司導入 AI 工具的時間點不同，研究比較「已導入」與「尚未導入」的公司，看導入前後的變化。
  • 區分兩種工具：自動補完型的 coding assistant，以及會自己接任務、產出修改的 coding agent。

二、結果：上游變多，下游沒動

導入 coding agent 之後，每位工程師平均：

指標變化
程式碼行數約 +30%（每月多近 1,500 行）
Commit 數約 +20%
Pull request 數約 +23%
完成的 Jira issue沒有統計上顯著的變化

公司層級的人數也沒有因此明顯減少。作者的結論是：生產力的提升，沒有完整傳遞到軟體產出或人力上，而是被流程下游的限制吸收掉了。

三、被吸收到哪裡？Code Review

報導裡最有意思的是 review 端的數字：

  • PR 從送出到合併的 review 時間增加約 49%
  • 被要求修改的 PR 比例幾乎翻倍
  • 每個 PR 的 review 留言數增加約 35%
  • 參與 code review 的工程師比例增加約 14%

換句話說，寫程式變快了，但 review 的人變忙、退件變多、等待變長。到 2026 年 3 月，約 80% 的公司已經在用某種 AI code review，但 AI 只貢獻了 23.3% 的 review 留言、出現在 10.8% 的 PR 上——review 這一段，主要還是靠人。

作者的建議也很明確：要拿到 AI 的效益，需要同步投資下游的 review 能力，而不是只追求更多程式碼。

四、我怎麼解讀：這不是「AI 沒用」

這份研究很容易被讀成「AI 寫 code 是假的」。我不這麼看。它真正說的是：軟體交付是一條產線，只加速其中一站，整條線的速度由最慢的那站決定。

這和我在 AI 導入實戰 裡談的原則一樣：自動化可以接手執行，但驗收與權限要留在人手上。而一旦執行變便宜，驗收就成了新的瓶頸。

需要注意的限制：

  • 這是工作論文，還沒經過同儕審查。
  • 「完成的 issue 數」是很粗的產出指標，品質、可維護性、事故率都沒算進去。
  • 資料截至 2026 年 3 月，之後的 agent 與 AI review 工具又進步了不少。

五、給團隊的四個調整

1. 不要再用行數和 commit 數衡量效益

研究直接點出，很多主管依賴這類中間指標。導入 agent 後它們一定會漲，但那不代表交付變多。改看 lead time（從開單到上線）、每個 PR 的 review 等待時間、退件率。

2. 讓 PR 變小、變好審

agent 很容易一次改一大片。在指引或 AGENTS.md 裡寫清楚：一個 PR 只做一件事、附上驗證步驟、說明改了什麼與為什麼。好審的 PR 比多寫的程式碼更有價值。

3. 把機械性檢查交給 CI，人只看判斷題

型別、lint、測試、建置、安全掃描，全部在 PR 進到人手上之前跑完。人的 review 時間留給架構、邊界條件和商業邏輯——也就是我在 Code Review Checklist 裡列的那些。

4. 把 review 當成正式產能來規劃

如果團隊導入 agent 後產出多了兩成 PR，review 的時間就要跟著編列，而不是默默壓在資深工程師的下班時間上。AI review 可以先過濾，但最後的放行要有明確的負責人。

AI 工具讓「寫出程式碼」變便宜了，真正的競爭力轉移到「確認它是對的、然後安全地交付」。如果你的團隊導入 AI 後感覺很忙、但上線速度沒有變快，可以預約 30 分鐘初談，一起找出卡住的那一站。

title: From a biomedical lab to AI architect: my cross-domain path
summary: I studied food science, did gene sequencing in grad school, taught myself to code, and now design AI platforms. The first post in my career journey series lays out this not-so-straight path and what each stage left me with.
html:
From a biomedical lab to AI architect

People often ask me, "Didn't you study biology? How did you end up as an engineer?"

The answer doesn't fit in one sentence, so I started a "Career journey" category to write it out over time. This is the first post, and it lays out the whole route. For the full timeline, see my career path.

1. The start: learning on my own, on a path others expected

I've always liked figuring things out myself. Growing up I entered art competitions and was in a choir and an art class, and I developed an instinctive, stubborn sense for aesthetics and design.

At university I studied food science at National Taiwan Ocean University, which is mostly biology and chemistry. My grades were fine, but the further I went, the clearer it was that this wasn't what I wanted to do long term. I had already started teaching myself web development, though I hadn't thought of it as a career yet.

2. The turning point: my first real system, built in a biomedical grad program

For my master's I joined the Institute of Molecular Medicine and Bioengineering at National Chiao Tung University, working in the dean's computer science lab on gene sequencing and bioinformatics, analyzing data in R and Python every day. My thesis was a testing tool for chronic kidney disease.

The real turning point came in a computer science elective. I built a front-end and back-end integration for a class project, the professor was impressed, and real client work started coming my way.

From there I worked my way from HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PHP to Angular, React, Vue and Express.js. With no computer science degree, I had to build my skills one project at a time.

3. Alternative military service: a second job after hours

During my alternative military service, I spent every evening filling gaps in computer science fundamentals, building a portfolio, and starting my own brand, "1914." One project from that time was a customer service chatbot with intent recognition, connected to LINE, Facebook chatbots and Google Dialogflow and deployed on Heroku.

Looking back, it was the first time I took an idea all the way to something other people could actually use.

4. Into the industry: starting in the back end, across four kinds of work

After my service I deliberately went for a pure back-end engineering role, passed the assessment, and was given plenty of room to explore. Over the eight-plus years since, I've worked roughly in these settings:

SettingWhat I learned there
Enterprise systemsModernizing legacy systems: separate front and back ends, CI/CD, security scanning
E-commerce and SaaSHigh traffic and reliability: millions of push notifications an hour, SLAs, blue-green deployment, multi-cloud
Finance and manufacturingDelivering under strict constraints: container platforms, microservices, integration with large systems such as SAP
International teamsMulti-system integration, and leading the user experience design of a POS

Today I work on AI platform architecture: RAG, on-premises model services, AI agents, and getting these services into real use.

Throughout, I've also taken freelance work across design, front end and back end, which gradually filled out my UI/UX and full-stack skills.

5. Three things crossing fields left me with

If I had to answer "did studying biology help you as an engineer?" in one sentence: yes, and more so the further I go.

1. A lab habit: verify before you believe

In research, a result without a control group that can't be reproduced doesn't count. That habit came straight into engineering: verification steps before launch, and monitoring that tells you what went wrong.

In the age of AI this matters even more. RAG and AI agents produce convincing output, so whether you can evaluate it and prove it's right decides whether it can go live.

2. An art background: interfaces should be understood at a glance

Art training as a kid made me sensitive to whether something looks right and flows well. That became my standard for experience design: a good interface needs no manual, and it should be accessible and use readable type.

3. Teaching myself: nobody teaches you the next technology

Without a computer science degree, I had to find answers and build things myself from day one. The technology keeps changing, from jQuery to React, from virtual machines to Kubernetes, and now to LLMs. What carries over isn't any one framework. It's the ability to learn something new quickly and get it to the point where it can ship.

6. The biggest lesson of these years

Good architecture creates long-term value for a business, far more than the short-term gain of rushing to launch.

I only really understood this after high-traffic e-commerce and the strict rules of finance. Many problems aren't bugs in the code. They come from not thinking through how the data flows and how to roll back when something breaks.

7. Outside of work

I still have a lot of interests: singing lessons, gymnastics classes, and I'm a certified spin instructor. I also enjoy being a couch potato with a good series. For me, the rhythm of life outside work is what keeps the work sustainable.

What I plan to write next

This series will unfold one stage at a time. Topics I have in mind so far:

  • How I planned self-study and a portfolio without a computer science degree
  • What switching from biomedicine to engineering actually looked like: résumé, interviews and the first job
  • What each industry taught me about engineering: e-commerce, finance, manufacturing
  • Moving from engineer to architect: what actually changes in the work

If you're considering a career change across fields, or you're curious about any of these topics, subscribe for updates or book a time to talk.

title: 從生醫實驗室到 AI 架構師：我的跨領域路線
summary: 大學念食品科學，研究所做基因定序，後來一路自學成為工程師，現在做 AI 平台架構。職涯歷程系列的第一篇，先把這條不太直的路整理一遍，以及每一段留下了什麼。
html:
從生醫實驗室到 AI 架構師

常有人問我：「你不是念生物的嗎？怎麼會變成工程師？」

這個問題一句話講不完，所以我開了「職涯歷程」這個分類，打算慢慢寫。這是第一篇，先把整條路線攤開來。完整的時間軸可以看職涯路徑。

一、起點：喜歡自己學，但走的是別人期待的路

我從小就喜歡自己摸索。常參加美術比賽、待過合唱團和美術班，對美感和設計有一種直覺上的執著。

大學念的是海洋大學食品科學系，主軸是生物與化學。成績不差，但越讀越清楚：這不是我想長期投入的方向。那時候已經開始自學寫網頁，只是還沒想過能當成工作。

二、轉折：在生醫研究所寫出第一個被採用的系統

研究所進了交大分子醫學與生物工程所，待在院長的資工實驗室，做基因定序與生物資訊分析，每天用 R 和 Python 處理資料。碩士論文做的是慢性腎臟病的檢驗工具。

真正的轉折發生在一堂資工選修課。我在課堂專案裡完成了一個前後端整合的需求，教授很肯定，之後開始有實際的案子找上門。

從那時起，我從 HTML、CSS、JavaScript、PHP 一路學到 Angular、React、Vue 和 Express.js。沒有資工學位，只能靠一個一個案子把能力補起來。

三、替代役：下班後的第二份工作

替代役期間，我每天下班後補資工基礎、做作品集，也建立了自己的品牌「1914」。那段時間做過一個語意辨識的客服機器人：串接 LINE、Facebook Chatbot 和 Google Dialogflow，部署在 Heroku 上。

現在回頭看，那是我第一次把「一個想法」從頭做到「別人真的能用」。

四、進入業界：從後端開始，一路走過四種產業

退伍後，我刻意挑戰純後端工程師的職缺，通過考核，也得到不少技術探索的空間。之後八年多，大致走過這幾種場域：

場域我在那裡學到的事
企業系統把老舊系統現代化：前後端分離、CI/CD、資安掃描
電商與 SaaS高流量與穩定性：每小時數百萬則推播、SLA、藍綠部署、多雲架構
金融與製造在嚴格環境裡交付：容器平台、微服務、與 SAP 等大型系統整合
跨國團隊多系統整合，以及主導 POS 的操作體驗設計

現在的工作是 AI 平台架構：RAG、地端模型服務、AI Agent，以及讓這些服務真正落地。

這段期間我也一直有接案，從設計、前端到後端都做，慢慢長出比較完整的 UI/UX 與全端能力。

五、跨領域留下的三件事

如果只能用一句話回答「念生物對當工程師有沒有幫助」，我的答案是：有，而且越到後面越明顯。

1. 實驗室的習慣：先驗證，再相信

做研究時，一個結果沒有對照組、不能重現，就不算數。這個習慣直接帶進了工程：上線前要有驗證步驟、監控要能告訴你出了什麼事。

到了 AI 時代，這件事更重要。RAG 和 AI Agent 的輸出看起來都很有說服力，能不能評測、能不能證明它是對的，才是能不能上線的關鍵。

2. 美術背景：介面要讓人看過就會用

小時候的美術訓練，讓我對「好不好看、順不順」很敏感。這後來變成我對體驗設計的堅持：好的介面不需要說明書，還要兼顧無障礙與易讀的字體。

3. 自學的能力：沒有人會教你下一個技術

我沒有資工學位，所以從第一天起就習慣自己找資料、自己做出來。技術一直在換，從 jQuery 到 React，從虛擬機到 Kubernetes，再到現在的 LLM。真正能帶著走的，不是某個框架，而是快速學會一件新事情、並把它做到能交付的能力。

六、這幾年最大的體悟

良好的架構設計能為企業創造長期價值，遠勝於匆忙上線的短期收益。

這句話是走過電商的高流量、金融的嚴格規範之後才真正體會到的。很多問題不是程式寫錯，而是一開始就沒有想清楚資料怎麼流、出事時怎麼退。

七、工作之外

我還是那個興趣很多的人：上歌唱課、體操課，也拿到了飛輪教練執照。當然也很享受當沙發馬鈴薯追劇。對我來說，生活的節奏是讓工作能長期走下去的能量來源。

接下來想寫的

這個系列之後會一段一段展開，目前想到的有：

  • 沒有資工學位，我怎麼規劃自學與作品集
  • 從生醫轉職工程師的實際過程：履歷、面試與第一份工作
  • 每一種產業帶給我的工程觀：電商、金融、製造
  • 從工程師走向架構師，工作內容到底差在哪

如果你也正在考慮跨領域轉職，或對其中哪個主題特別好奇，歡迎訂閱更新，或預約時間聊聊。

title: The Node.js October security release: 10 CVEs, 4 high, and a good moment to check whether your Node is already EOL
summary: On October 21 Node.js shipped security releases for the 22, 24 and 26 lines, fixing TLS hostname verification bypasses, a Brotli out-of-bounds write and more. Which version to move to, who should move first, and the EOL version I found on my own machine.
html:
The Node.js October security release

Last week I wrote about Next.js 16.4 and the October security update, and on October 21 Node.js published its own security release. This one reaches further: if your service, build or CI runs on Node, you are in scope.

1. The short version: move to one of these

LinePatched version
26.xv26.12.1
24.xv24.22.1
22.xv22.23.4

The highest severity on all three lines is High. There are no workarounds; the fix is to upgrade.

nvm install 24.22.1 && nvm alias default 24.22.1
node -v

2. What was fixed

Ten CVEs in total: 4 high, 3 medium, 3 low. I group them into three buckets.

1. TLS hostname verification bypasses (high and medium)

This is the group to pay attention to. With unusual spellings of an IP address, tls.checkServerIdentity() can validate a certificate against the wrong target:

  • IPs written with fullwidth digits (such as １２７.0.0.1), a regression after an earlier fix
  • IPv4 literals with a leading zero (such as 0127.0.0.1): URL parsing reads them as octal while the OS resolver reads them as decimal, so the two disagree on the address
  • Non-canonical forms such as 0x7f.0.0.1 or 127.1, which let a DNS-only certificate pass verification for an IP connection

Who should worry: services that make HTTPS requests to URLs or IPs taken from user input, such as webhooks, image proxies, link previews and crawlers. These are also where SSRF protection most often breaks.

2. Decompression and DNS edge cases (high)

  • Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write: malicious Brotli data can cause a crash, memory disclosure or even remote code execution. Any service that uses node:zlib to decompress outside data is affected.
  • dns.resolve*() truncates names at a NUL character: a follow-up to an incomplete earlier fix.

3. Also worth knowing

  • The random caches behind crypto.randomUUID() and friends could be saved into startup snapshots and SEAs, so every process produced the same values. Teams using --build-snapshot or single executable apps should take note.
  • Several Permission Model bypasses (low).
  • Dependency updates: c-ares, undici, OpenSSL (24 and 22), and removal of the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates.

3. What I found on my own machine

While writing this I ran node -v and got v23.11.0. Odd-numbered 23 has been end of life for a while. The official notice is explicit: EOL versions are always considered affected by a security release, and they get no fix.

This site runs on Cloudflare Workers in production, so these Node CVEs don't hit it directly. But builds, local development and parts of CI all run on Node. Your development machine is attack surface too, especially now that coding agents download packages and run commands on it for you.

That's a blind spot for many teams: someone looks after production, but nobody looks after laptops and CI runners.

4. An upgrade checklist for teams

  • Inventory which Node version runs in production, CI, Docker base images and developer machines
  • Replace odd-numbered (23, 25) and EOL versions with an LTS
  • Move to v24.22.1, v22.23.4 or v26.12.1
  • Add .nvmrc or engines in package.json so the version is a rule you can check
  • Pin Docker tags (for example node:24.22.1-slim) instead of node:24 that nobody remembers to rebuild
  • Review code that makes requests from user input and make sure URL and IP allowlists are checked after parsing
  • Run build, tests and smoke tests before going live

Two months in a row of security releases makes one thing clear: frameworks and runtimes are patched too often to rely on upgrading whenever someone remembers. A fixed monthly version check matters more than any single emergency upgrade. If you'd like help setting up that routine, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: Node.js 10 月安全更新：10 個 CVE、4 個 High，順便檢查你的 Node 是不是早就 EOL
summary: Node.js 在 10/21 為 22、24、26 三條線發布安全更新，修補 TLS 主機名驗證繞過、Brotli 越界寫入等問題。整理該升到哪一版、誰最該先升，以及我在自己電腦上發現的 EOL 版本。
html:
Node.js 10 月安全更新

上週才寫完 Next.js 16.4 與 10 月安全更新，10 月 21 日 Node.js 也發布了安全更新。這次範圍更廣：只要你的服務、建置或 CI 跑在 Node 上，都在影響範圍內。

一、先看結論：升到這三個版本

版本線修補版本
26.xv26.12.1
24.xv24.22.1
22.xv22.23.4

三條線的最高嚴重度都是 High。官方沒有提供替代方案，處理方式就是升級。

nvm install 24.22.1 && nvm alias default 24.22.1
node -v

二、這次修了什麼

一共 10 個 CVE：4 個 High、3 個 Medium、3 個 Low。我把它們歸成三類：

1. TLS 主機名驗證可被繞過（High／Medium）

這是這次最需要注意的一組。用特殊寫法表示 IP 位址時，tls.checkServerIdentity() 可能把憑證驗證成錯誤的對象：

  • 全形數字的 IP（例如 １２７.0.0.1）——這是先前修補後的回歸問題
  • 帶前導零的 IPv4（例如 0127.0.0.1），URL 解析當成八進位、系統解析器當成十進位，兩邊看到的位址不同
  • 0x7f.0.0.1、127.1 這類非標準寫法，讓只有 DNS 名稱的憑證通過 IP 連線的驗證

誰該緊張：會依使用者輸入的網址或 IP 發出 HTTPS 請求的服務，例如 webhook、圖片代理、URL 預覽、爬蟲。這些也是 SSRF 防護最常出問題的地方。

2. 解壓與 DNS 的邊界問題（High）

  • Brotli 解碼越界寫入：處理惡意的 Brotli 資料可能導致當機、記憶體洩漏，甚至遠端程式碼執行。任何會用 node:zlib 解壓外部資料的服務都受影響。
  • dns.resolve*() 遇到 NUL 字元會截斷名稱：先前修補不完整的延續。

3. 其他值得知道的

  • crypto.randomUUID() 等函式的亂數快取會被存進 startup snapshot 與 SEA，導致每個行程產生相同的值。有用 --build-snapshot 或單一執行檔打包的團隊要特別注意。
  • Permission Model 的幾個繞過問題（Low）。
  • 相依套件更新：c-ares、undici、OpenSSL（24／22），以及移除遭外洩的 eMudhra 中繼 CA 憑證。

三、我在自己電腦上發現的事

寫這篇時順手跑了一次 node -v，結果是 v23.11.0。23 是奇數版本，早就 EOL 了。官方公告寫得很清楚：EOL 版本在每次安全更新時一律視為受影響，而且不會有修補。

這個網站正式環境跑在 Cloudflare Workers 上，不直接受 Node 的這些 CVE 影響；但建置、本機開發、部分 CI 都跑在 Node 上。開發機本身就是攻擊面，尤其現在 coding agent 會在本機替你下載套件、執行指令。

這也是很多團隊的盲點：正式環境有人顧，開發機和 CI runner 沒人顧。

四、給團隊的升級清單

  • 盤點：正式環境、CI、Docker base image、開發機各跑哪個 Node 版本
  • 把奇數版本（23、25）與已 EOL 的版本換成 LTS
  • 升到 v24.22.1／v22.23.4／v26.12.1
  • 在專案加上 .nvmrc 或 package.json 的 engines，讓版本變成可檢查的規則
  • Docker 用明確的 tag（例如 node:24.22.1-slim），不要只寫 node:24 然後忘了重建
  • 檢查會依使用者輸入發出請求的程式，確認 URL／IP 白名單在解析後才比對
  • 跑過 build、測試與 smoke test 再上線

連續兩個月都在寫安全更新，說明了一件事：框架和執行環境的修補頻率已經高到不能靠「想到再升」。固定每月一次的版本盤點，比任何單次緊急升級都重要。如果你需要協助建立這套節奏，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: Google will support a shared AI training control: what site owners should set in robots.txt
summary: On October 30, Google announced it will support a shared, IETF-based AI training control in robots.txt, so one rule can tell every AI provider not to train on your content. It is planned for 2027. What it covers, what it does not, and what you can set today.
html:
Google will support a shared AI training control

On October 30, the Google Search Central blog published a short post: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites, by John Mueller. The point is simple: Google plans to support one robots.txt training control shared across AI providers.

For personal sites, blogs and portfolios, this is one of the few search announcements this year that actually affects you.

1. What it is

  • Mechanism: a shared "policy token" in robots.txt that says "do not use this site's content to train AI".
  • Origin: the IETF AIPREF working group (draft). It is not a Google-only spec.
  • Syntax: Google's crawler documentation currently refers to it as user-agent: __usage_ai-training. The spec is still a draft, so the final syntax may change.
  • Timing: Google says it aims to support it alongside other AI providers in 2027; the documentation says early 2027.

2. How it relates to Google-Extended

Google already has its own control, Google-Extended, which governs whether content is used for Gemini training and grounding. The shared control does not replace it:

  • If a site opts out with the shared token and does not mention Google-Extended, Google will treat it as if Google-Extended were disallowed.
  • If a site explicitly sets Google-Extended, that rule wins.
  • Each company's existing controls keep working.

Google's documentation is also clear that Google-Extended does not affect whether a site appears in Google Search and is not a ranking signal. So the worry that opting out of training hurts your ranking does not hold, at least on the Google-Extended side.

3. What it does not cover

This is the part most likely to be misread:

  • It controls training, not search. Whether you are indexed is still up to Googlebot.
  • The announcement does not mention AI Overviews or AI Mode. If you want to stay out of AI summaries entirely, this token is not the answer.
  • Conversely, Google notes that sites that explicitly allow Google-Extended are eligible to appear in Gemini Apps responses and receive clicks via grounding.

So there is a trade-off: opting out of training and grounding also means giving up being cited in Gemini answers.

4. What site owners can do now

1. Decide where you stand

Ask yourself: do I want AI to learn from my content and cite it?

  • Freelancers, consultants, personal brands: you usually want to be seen and cited. Stay open and put the effort into content quality.
  • Paid content, original work, photography and illustration: you may care more about training use and choose to opt out.

2. What works today: Google-Extended

If you want to stop Gemini from using your content, you can add this to robots.txt now:

User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /

You can also block only some paths. Google's own example allows a single page and blocks the rest of a directory.

3. Add the shared token once the spec is final

__usage_ai-training is still an IETF draft, and Google expects to support it in 2027. Note it now and add it when it is officially live, so you are not shipping a rule nobody reads.

4. On Next.js, robots lives in code

This site uses app/robots.ts. The current rules allow everything except the admin and tool pages. My position is open: these articles are meant to be read and cited, and the site also serves /llms.txt so AI tools can understand its structure more easily.

For the first time, there is a shared, cross-company language for how AI providers may use website content. It is not perfect and not live yet, but the direction is right: the decision goes back to the site owner. If you want your site's robots, sitemap and SEO setup reviewed, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: Google 宣布支援共通的 AI 訓練開關：網站主現在該怎麼設定 robots.txt
summary: Google 10/30 宣布將支援 IETF 提案的共通 AI 訓練控制，用 robots.txt 一次告訴各家 AI 業者「不要拿我的內容訓練模型」，預計 2027 年上線。整理它管什麼、不管什麼，以及現在可以先做的設定。
html:
Google 宣布支援共通的 AI 訓練開關

10 月 30 日，Google Search Central 部落格發了一篇短文：Supporting a shared AI training control for websites（John Mueller）。重點只有一個：Google 打算支援一個「各家 AI 業者共用」的 robots.txt 訓練控制。

對個人網站、部落格、作品集來說，這是今年少數真正跟你有關的搜尋消息。

一、它是什麼

  • 機制：寫在 robots.txt 裡的一個共通「policy token」，用來表達「不要拿這個網站的內容訓練 AI」。
  • 來源：IETF 的 AIPREF 工作小組（提案草稿）。不是 Google 自己的規格。
  • 寫法：Google 的爬蟲文件目前寫的是 user-agent: __usage_ai-training。規格還在草稿階段，正式寫法以上線時為準。
  • 時程：Google 說目標是 2027 年與其他 AI 業者一起支援，文件寫的是 2027 年初。

二、跟 Google-Extended 的關係

Google 早就有自己的開關 Google-Extended，用來控制內容是否用於 Gemini 的訓練與 grounding。新的共通開關不會取代它：

  • 網站用共通 token 拒絕訓練、而且沒有另外寫 Google-Extended → Google 會把它當成拒絕 Google-Extended。
  • 網站有明確寫 Google-Extended → 以 Google-Extended 的設定為準。
  • 各家既有的專屬開關會繼續有效。

另外，Google 文件寫得很清楚：**Google-Extended 不影響網站是否出現在 Google 搜尋，也不是排名訊號。**所以「關掉訓練會不會掉排名」這個擔心，至少在 Google-Extended 這一側是不成立的。

三、它不管什麼

這點最容易被誤會：

  • 它是訓練的開關，不是搜尋的開關。要不要被 Google 搜尋收錄，還是由 Googlebot 決定。
  • 公告沒有提到 AI Overviews 或 AI Mode。如果你希望完全不出現在 AI 摘要裡，這個 token 不是答案。
  • 反過來，Google 提到：明確允許 Google-Extended 的網站，才有資格透過 grounding 出現在 Gemini Apps 的回答裡並獲得點擊。

所以這是取捨：拒絕訓練與 grounding，就放棄了在 Gemini 回答中被引用的機會。

四、網站主現在可以怎麼做

1. 先決定立場

問自己：我希望 AI 學我的內容、引用我嗎？

  • 接案者、顧問、個人品牌：通常希望被看見、被引用。保持開放，把力氣放在內容品質上。
  • 付費內容、原創作品、攝影與插畫：可能更在意被拿去訓練。可以考慮拒絕。

2. 今天就能用的設定：Google-Extended

如果你想拒絕 Gemini 使用內容，現在就能在 robots.txt 加上：

User-agent: Google-Extended
Disallow: /

也可以只擋部分路徑，例如 Google 文件的範例是允許單一頁、擋整個目錄。

3. 共通 token 等規格定案再加

__usage_ai-training 還在 IETF 草稿階段，Google 預計 2027 年才支援。現在可以先記下來，等正式公告再上，避免寫了一個沒人讀的規則。

4. 用 Next.js 的話，robots 寫在程式裡

8plus 這個網站用的是 app/robots.ts，目前規則是全部允許、只擋後台與工具頁。我的立場是開放：這裡的文章本來就是希望被讀到、被引用；網站也另外提供 /llms.txt，讓 AI 工具更容易讀懂網站結構。

AI 業者用什麼內容、怎麼用，終於開始有一個跨公司的共通語言。它還不完美，也還沒上線，但方向是對的：**決定權回到網站主手上。**如果你想檢查自己網站的 robots、sitemap 與 SEO 設定，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。

title: GitHub Octoverse 2026: agents start 40% of pull requests. Change the process, not the headcount
summary: GitHub's Octoverse 2026 report says more than 40% of pull requests in September started with a coding agent, up from 17% in March. The numbers that matter for teams, and four things to change first.
html:
GitHub Octoverse 2026: agents start 40% of pull requests

On October 28, GitHub published its annual Octoverse 2026 report. The line everyone is quoting: as of September, more than 40% of pull requests start with an agent. In March it was 17%.

Last week I wrote about a Harvard study showing AI agents produce 30% more code without shipping more software. Octoverse looks at the same shift from a different angle: not the payoff for one team, but the traffic on the whole platform.

1. The scale

The report covers October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, across public and private repositories:

Metric20252026
Pushes6.7B17.9B
Commits12.9B34.3B
Merged pull requests538M1.3B (3.5M a day on average)
GitHub Actions jobs14.0B45.4B

There were more pushes this year than in 2024 and 2025 combined, and GitHub now has more than 225 million developers.

2. Five numbers about agents

  1. More than 40% of pull requests start with an agent (17% in March). GitHub counts a pull request when its first draft came from a coding agent it can detect, so undetected use is not included.
  2. Agent pull requests now merge more often. In February, 83% of agent-involved pull requests merged within two weeks, slightly behind roughly 86% for the rest. By September, agent pull requests were at 90% while the comparison group held at about 86%.
  3. Agent pull requests touch more files. About 87% change multiple files, compared with 79% of other pull requests.
  4. TypeScript is still the top language by contributors, followed by Python and JavaScript. Among repositories created in 2026, TypeScript was the primary language in 35% of those with an agent signal, versus 24% without one.
  5. Review tooling is growing too. Use of AI-assisted code review and GitHub Advanced Security each grew more than 90% year over year, and 55% of Copilot's monthly active users now use agentic features (35% a year ago).

One more observation I found interesting: among repositories created this year, those with an agent configuration file (such as AGENTS.md) logged eight times as many commits as those without one. That does not mean the file causes the output. More likely, teams that take agents seriously also take the time to configure them.

3. How I read it

A higher merge rate is not proof of quality

Agent pull requests went from trailing to leading on two-week merge rate. You can read that as "agents are getting better", or as "reviewers are getting used to approving them". The report measures merges, not incidents or rollbacks after the merge. Good news, but not a conclusion.

Multi-file changes are where review costs go up

87% of agent pull requests touch several files, and cross-file changes are where side effects hide. This lines up with the Harvard finding that review time and change requests went up. When writing code gets cheap, the pressure moves downstream.

TypeScript's lead will keep growing

Types act as both a spec and a check for agents. When an agent gets something wrong, tsc catches it before a person has to. If your team is still undecided between plain JavaScript and TypeScript, this is one more reason.

4. Four things teams can change first

1. Write an AGENTS.md

Spell out project conventions, the commands to install, test and build, the directories that are off limits, and the PR format. It is the cheapest way to get agent output that looks like your team wrote it. This site has one too.

2. Keep pull requests small

Tell agents to do one thing per pull request and include verification steps. GitHub's stacked pull requests (preview since July 30, used by more than 264,000 developers by September) exist for exactly this: splitting a large change into reviewable pieces.

3. Measure what happens after the merge

Alongside merge rate, track rollbacks, bugs within seven days of release, and hotfixes. Those show the real quality of agent pull requests.

4. Let CI do the mechanical checks

Types, lint, tests and secret scanning should all pass before a pull request reaches a person. Push protection scans rose sharply in the report for a simple reason: the faster code is produced, the more chances there are to push a secret by mistake.

Agent-started pull requests went from under a fifth to over two fifths in six months. What separates teams now is how they review, verify and gate that work. If you want to set up agent guidelines and a review process for your team, book a 30-minute intro call.

title: GitHub Octoverse 2026：四成 PR 由 Agent 起手，團隊該調整的是流程，不是人數
summary: GitHub 10 月底發布 Octoverse 2026：9 月有超過 40% 的 pull request 由 coding agent 起手，3 月時只有 17%。整理報告裡跟團隊最相關的數字，以及接下來該先改的四件事。
html:
GitHub Octoverse 2026：四成 PR 由 Agent 起手

10 月 28 日，GitHub 發布年度報告 Octoverse 2026。最常被引用的一句是：到了 9 月，超過 40% 的 pull request 是用 agent 起手的；3 月時還只有 17%。

上週我寫了哈佛研究：AI agent 讓程式碼多三成，交付卻沒變多。Octoverse 剛好是同一件事的另一個角度——不是單一團隊的效益，而是整個平台的流量。

一、先看規模

報告的統計區間是 2025/10/1 到 2026/9/30，數字包含公開與私有 repo：

指標20252026
Push 次數67 億179 億
Commit 數129 億343 億
合併的 PR5.38 億13 億（平均每天 350 萬）
GitHub Actions 工作140 億454 億

一年的 push 數，比 2024 和 2025 加起來還多。GitHub 上的開發者超過 2.25 億人。

二、和 agent 有關的五個數字

  1. 超過 40% 的 PR 由 agent 起手（3 月是 17%）。GitHub 的定義是「第一版草稿來自可偵測到的 coding agent」，偵測不到的使用不會算進去。
  2. agent PR 的合併率追上來了：2 月時，agent 參與的 PR 有 83% 在兩週內合併，略低於一般 PR 的約 86%；到了 9 月，agent PR 是 90%，一般 PR 仍約 86%。
  3. agent PR 更常一次改很多檔案：約 87% 動到多個檔案，一般 PR 是 79%。
  4. TypeScript 仍是貢獻者最多的語言，Python、JavaScript 分居二、三。2026 年新開、有 agent 跡象的 repo 中，35% 以 TypeScript 為主，沒有 agent 跡象的只有 24%。
  5. review 工具跟著長：AI 輔助 code review 與 GitHub Advanced Security 的使用量都比去年多了 90% 以上。Copilot 的月活躍使用者中，55% 用了 agent 功能（一年前是 35%）。

另外一個我覺得有意思的觀察：今年新開的 repo 裡，**有 agent 設定檔（例如 AGENTS.md）的 repo，平均 commit 數是沒有的八倍。**這不代表設定檔造成產出變多，比較可能是「認真用 agent 的團隊，也會認真寫設定」。

三、我怎麼解讀

合併率上升，不等於品質沒問題

agent PR 的兩週合併率從落後變成領先，可以讀成「agent 寫得越來越好」，也可以讀成「review 越來越習慣放行」。報告本身只量測合併，不量測合併後的事故或回滾。所以這個數字是好消息，但不是結論。

「一次改很多檔」是 review 的成本

87% 的 agent PR 動到多個檔案。對 reviewer 來說，跨檔案的修改最難看出副作用。這和哈佛研究看到的「review 時間變長、退件變多」是同一個方向：上游變便宜，壓力就往下游跑。

TypeScript 的優勢會繼續擴大

型別本身就是給 agent 的規格與檢查。agent 寫錯，tsc 會先擋下來，人不必花時間抓低階錯誤。如果團隊還在純 JavaScript 和 TypeScript 之間猶豫，這份數據又多了一個理由。

四、團隊可以先改的四件事

1. 寫一份 AGENTS.md

把專案慣例、指令（安裝、測試、建置）、不准碰的目錄、PR 格式寫清楚。這是讓 agent 產出「接近你團隊寫法」最便宜的方法。8plus 這個網站自己也有一份。

2. 限制 PR 範圍

在指引裡要求 agent 一個 PR 只做一件事，並附上驗證步驟。GitHub 今年推出的 stacked pull requests（7 月底預覽，到 9 月已有超過 26.4 萬名開發者用過）就是為了讓大改動拆成小段審查。

3. 量合併之後的事

除了合併率，也追蹤回滾次數、上線後 7 天內的 bug、hotfix 數量。這些才看得出 agent PR 的真實品質。

4. 讓 CI 先擋，人看判斷題

型別、lint、測試、secret 掃描在 PR 到人手上之前全部跑完。報告裡 push protection 的掃描量今年大增，原因也很直接：程式碼產得越快，金鑰誤推的機會越多。

agent 起手的 PR 從兩成不到變成四成，只花了半年。真正拉開差距的，會是團隊怎麼審、怎麼驗、怎麼把關。如果你想替團隊建立 agent 協作的規範與 review 流程，可以預約 30 分鐘初談。
